title: IoT Report through the API: REST, Z-Insights GraphQL, SDKs, MCP

prose.text: There are two ways to read IoT data programmatically, with different contents: the ZIA REST endpoints give the device inventory, and Z-Insights GraphQL gives counts.

prose.label: REST (per device).
prose.text: {{rest-endpoints}} {{no-write-operations}} {{taxonomy-response-shape}} {{device-list-shape}} {{device-names-from-taxonomy}} What the levels and UUIDs mean is in [[zia.iot.classification]].
The inventory is only as complete as location discovery allows: [[zia.iot.discovery]]. Which role the REST calls need is open {{gap:rest-permissions}}.

checks.do: Which role the REST calls need, since the integration test for them may fail on permissions.

rest-endpoints.statement: Four read-only GET endpoints under the ZIA API back the report: /iotDiscovery/deviceTypes, /iotDiscovery/categories, /iotDiscovery/classifications and /iotDiscovery/deviceList.

expect.operationId: Iot Discovery Resource Get Device Types
Iot Discovery Resource Get Device List

no-write-operations.statement: The IoT Report has no create, update or delete operation: the OpenAPI spec lists only GET for these paths and the Go SDK exposes only four read functions.
no-write-operations.conditions: Rests on a search: the spec paths carry only a get member, and iotreport.go defines only the four Get functions.

taxonomy-response-shape.statement: The three taxonomy endpoints each return an array of objects with `uuid`, `name` and `parent_uuid`; `parent_uuid` does not apply to device types.

expect.description:
The parent UUID of the item.

Note: This field is not applicable for the device types endpoint.

device-list-shape.statement: deviceList returns an object with `cloudName`, `customerId` and a `devices` array; each device has `locationId`, `deviceUuid`, `ipAddress`, `deviceTypeUuid`, `autoLabel`, `classificationUuid`, `categoryUuid`, and `flowStartTime` and `flowEndTime` as epoch-second integers.

quotes: The start timestamp at which Zscaler AI/ML engine starts evaluating the device's weblog records. It's noted in epoch seconds.
The end timestamp at which Zscaler AI/ML engine stops evaluating the device's weblog records. It's noted in epoch seconds.

go-taxonomy-decodes-into-struct.statement: The Go SDK's GetDeviceTypes, GetIOTCategories and GetIOTClassifications decode the response into a single `CommonIOTReport` struct, but the endpoints return arrays, so the decode would be expected to fail rather than return the taxonomy. Use the REST call for the taxonomy.
go-taxonomy-decodes-into-struct.conditions: Derived from reading: the OpenAPI response is an array and the Go client unmarshals the body straight into the struct. Not run against a tenant; encoding/json rejects an array into a struct.

evidence.after: func (c *Client) Read(ctx context.Context, endpoint string, o interface{}) error {

no-terraform.statement: The ZIA Terraform provider has no resource or data source for the IoT Report. Its only IoT surface is the IoT flags on the location management resource (`iot_discovery_enabled` and `iot_enforce_policy_set`) and, on the location data source, `iot_discovery_enabled` alone, which is read back (`d.Set`); the data source does not expose `iot_enforce_policy_set`.
no-terraform.conditions: Rests on a search of the pinned provider for IoT-named resources and data sources, and on the location data source containing no iot_enforce_policy_set.

graphql-device-stats.statement: The Z-Insights GraphQL API has an IOT domain whose `device_stats` query returns `devices_count`, `iot_devices_count`, `user_devices_count`, `server_devices_count`, `un_classified_devices_count` and `entries` (each with `classifications`, `classification_uuid`, `category` and `total`).

quotes: classifications classification_uuid category total } devices_count user_devices_count iot_devices_count server_devices_count un_classified_devices_count
- entries: List of device classifications with totals

graphql-aggregates-only.statement: device_stats returns aggregate counts and per-classification totals, not per-device records.
graphql-aggregates-only.conditions: Derived from the query: its selection set holds only counts and entries, with no IP address or device fields; per-device data is REST deviceList.

graphql-filter-order.statement: `filter_by` accepts `classifications`, `classification_uuid` and `category`, each a StringFilter (`eq`, `ne`, `in_list`, `nin` in the Python SDK); `order_by` accepts `classifications`, `classification_uuid`, `category` and `total`.

quotes: classifications: Filter by device classification using StringFilter.
classification_uuid: Filter by classification UUID using StringFilter.
category: Filter by device category using StringFilter.
ne: Not equals - exclude exact string match.
in_list: In - match any string in the list.
nin: Not in - exclude any string in the list.
total: Sort order for the total field.

graphql-no-time-window.statement: The IOT device_stats query takes no start or end time: it reflects the present network state, not a time-windowed log slice.

quotes: No time window — this reflects the present network state.

graphql-role.statement: A Z-Insights GraphQL API client is registered with Authentication Service and given a role; the default role is Zscaler Insights Reader.

quotes: ensure that you have registered the API client with Authentication Service and selected an appropriate role for the client.
Authentication Service provides a default Zscaler Insights Reader role.

graphql-role.conditions: Corrected on recapture (2026-10-18): previously "A Z-Insights GraphQL API client is registered in ZIdentity with a role; the default role is Zscaler Insights Reader."

mcp-tool.statement: The MCP tool `zins_get_iot_device_stats` is read-only, takes only `limit` (1 to 1000, default 50) and returns the single stats object with the per-classification `entries`. An empty or zeroed result means no IoT devices were detected or IoT Device Visibility is not enabled.

quotes: Get IoT device statistics and classifications. Read-only analytics.
An empty/zeroed result means no IoT devices were detected or IoT Device Visibility is not enabled.

device-names-from-taxonomy.statement: The deviceList records carry only UUIDs for device type, category and classification, so their names come from joining to the three taxonomy lists, which return name with uuid.
device-names-from-taxonomy.conditions: Assumes the UUIDs in the device record are the same identifiers as the taxonomy uuid values; the field names suggest it but no source says it.

rest-permissions.title: What role or entitlement the /iotDiscovery REST endpoints need
rest-permissions.blocks: diagnosing a permission error from the IoT REST endpoints
rest-permissions.detail: The Python SDK integration test for all four calls is commented as one that may fail due to permission restrictions and is written to tolerate an error, which suggests a gate beyond a baseline credential. Unverified legacy statement: that the endpoints are gated behind an entitlement or role not present in a baseline ZIA credential, and that the Zscaler Insights Reader role applies only to the GraphQL path. No source names the role or entitlement for the REST path.

quotes: # Test get_device_types - may fail due to permission restrictions
